description.text: Publio Morbiducci (28 August 1889 – 31 March 1963) was an Italian sculptor whose career spanned the interwar period and the early years of the Italian Republic. He gained national recognition for his monumental works that were commissioned by the Mussolini government, and his art was even entered into the sculpture event of the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin.

Among his most celebrated commissions were the large‑scale sculptures for the Monument to the Bersaglieri at Porta Pia in 1932, the marble frieze of the Palazzo degli Uffici in the EUR district completed in 1939, and the bronze Discus Thrower at Rest that was added to the Stadio dei Marmi in 1938. In 1937 he was elected to the prestigious Accademia di San Luca, cementing his status as a leading figure in Italian sculpture of the early twentieth century.

curiosities.text: He participated in the art competition at the 1936 Summer Olympics.
He was named to the Accademia di San Luca in 1937.
He completed most of the sculptures of the Monument to the Bersaglieri in 1932.
He created the Discus Thrower at Rest that was added to the Stadio dei Marmi in 1938.
He completed the marble frieze of the Palazzo degli Uffici all'EUR in 1939.
